references.text: When Laban heard about Abraham's servant, he ran out to meet him and brought him home – a clear parallel to how Laban receives Jacob in Gen 29:13.
Esau ran to meet Jacob, embraced him, and kissed him – almost identical wording to Laban's welcome of Jacob, illustrating the Eastern greeting between relatives.
Jacob's conversation with the shepherds about Laban and his daughter Rachel leads directly up to the meeting with Laban in verse 13.
Laban's reaction when Jacob leaves without telling him stands in contrast to the warm welcome he gave Jacob upon his arrival.
Rebekah runs home and tells what has happened – paralleling how Jacob told Laban 'all these things' in Gen 29:13.
The dramatic reunion between father and son (Laban/Jacob) serves as a clear foreshadowing of the Father's gracious welcome of the prodigal son.
A deep thematic parallel about reunion and reconciliation after a break, where the kiss marks the end of the conflict.
